title: WHY DO YOU QUARREL WITH ME?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So they quarreled with Moses and said, 'Give us water to drink.' Moses replied,
'Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you put the LORD to the test?'"
- Ex 17:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the escalation. In chapter 16 they grumbled. Here they quarrel, and the
demand is blunt: "Give us water."

Moses asks two questions, and the second one exposes what is really happening.
"Why do you put the LORD to the test?"

There is a difference between asking God for something and testing God.
Scripture invites us to ask constantly, boldly, even desperately. The Psalms are
full of it. Testing is different. Testing says: prove Yourself, or I am done.

The distinction is not about how strongly we feel. It is about posture. Asking
comes from dependence. Testing comes from suspicion, and it puts God on trial
with ourselves as judge.

Notice too who they turned on. Moses, again. The one who had led them out.
People under pressure often attack whoever is nearest and most visible, and
leaders absorb a great deal of anger that is not really about them.

If you serve or lead others in any capacity, this is worth knowing. Some of the
frustration aimed at you is not truly yours to carry. Moses learned to take it
to God, as the next verses show.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you asking God for something, or quietly testing Him?
2. Who do you turn on when you are under pressure?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep me from putting You on trial. Teach me to ask boldly while trusting
You completely. Amen.
